judgments.rationale: The solution applies standard limits and L’Hôpital differentiation; the extra logarithm/function labels are notation, not independently assessed methods.
The markscheme differentiates a Maclaurin series and compares it with the tan² identity, so limits/series and differentiation are the assessed methods.
The integral test and the subsequent substitution/integration are explicitly marked; differentiation, logarithms and generic sequence labels add no separate method.
The solution uses the homogeneous-ODE substitution, integrates, and applies the initial condition; differential equations and integration are the material skills.
The proof bounds a definite integral and then establishes positivity/decrease and convergence of the sequence; integration and limits/series are retained.
Euclid’s algorithm, linear Diophantine solutions, and prime-factor LCM work earn algebraic-manipulation and equation-solving marks.
The marks require nearest-neighbour, deleted-vertex and Kruskal graph algorithms; the legacy graph-theory skill is the only honest controlled match.
Definitions and conclusions concern circuits, Eulerian trails/circuits, and graph complements; these require the legacy graph-theory skill.
The recurrence is solved via its characteristic quadratic and root form; sequences/series and quadratics are directly assessed.
Set listing, symmetric difference, intersections/unions and distributivity are explicitly marked, warranting the legacy sets skill.
Nearly all marks prove injectivity/surjectivity of a function and obtain its inverse, making Functions and inverses primary.
The estimator/test uses unbiased estimates, a t statistic, degrees of freedom and a normal model; descriptive arithmetic is supporting work.
The markscheme differentiates a continuous CDF to obtain a pdf, integrates for moments, and applies the CLT; integration is a calculus secondary method.
The PGF and its derivative are used for a discrete random variable and its linear transform; discrete random variables are the only material label.
Unbiasedness and variance identify the estimator, while differentiating its variance finds the minimum; inference is primary and optimization differentiation is secondary.
The hypotheses, p-value interpretation and recovery of t and r are all statistical-inference work; probability models is redundant.
The density normalization, summary measures, quartiles and conditional probability are marked; the normalizing definite integral is a calculus secondary method.
Graph/asymptote/reflection marks establish the function focus, while the definite integral and enclosed-area calculation independently assess integration applications.
Factor theorem, factorization, a quadratic complex-root calculation, graphing and concavity/derivative behavior are separate marked components owned by three topics.
The solution counts block arrangements and then uses a binomial model for repeated games; both probability and counting are independently marked.
The solution uses the union/intersection probability identity to find k and a complement probability; algebra is only routine rearrangement.
The cosine-rule quadratic, triangle solutions, area and discriminant/range argument are all triangle-geometry work.
Distance is obtained by integrating velocity over time, including a second definite integral to determine the height; integration applications and integration are primary.
Implicit differentiation supplies the gradient and tangent equation; the logarithm in the curve is not an independently assessed log method.
The region’s area is set up and evaluated with definite integrals; inverse-function notation only supports the setup.
The Poisson model gives the first probability and a binomial model gives the number of qualifying rooms; discrete random variables are the assessed method.
Reflection, vertical stretch and translation are each explicitly marked in the transformed graph equation, so both transformation skills are material.
Segment area in radians is the geometric core, followed by a marked related-rate derivative; the latter belongs in Calculus.
Each part standardizes a normal variable or finds a normal quantile; broad probability-model and descriptive labels are redundant.
The window maximum is found by differentiating the area, locating a stationary point and checking it is a maximum; no radian skill is marked.
The range, inverse formula, and inverse domain/range are all direct function-inverse work; inequality notation is incidental.
The particle-at-rest times and displacement are obtained from the derivative and stationary-time analysis, so Applications of differentiation is sufficient.
The square’s coordinates are found from complex-plane geometry and arithmetic with complex numbers; geometric transformations are not separately assessed.
The marked work is a tangent substitution followed by evaluation of an integral; trigonometric identities support rather than independently constitute the method.
Poisson probabilities are primary; solving the exponential equations in m and simplifying logarithms earns a secondary exponents/logarithms label.
The markscheme explicitly requires base case, induction hypothesis and induction step; binomial notation is enabling algebra, not a separate expansion method.
The sketches use graph transformations, integration by parts is marked, and g′ establishes monotonicity via differentiation; these map to the proposed topics.
The continuous pdf/moments/median and the binomial count are separately marked, with integration used for continuous moments.
Factor-theorem/factorization marks establish the polynomial topic, while the graph and range are a separate Functions secondary component.
Implicit differentiation and normal-line work are marked in part (a), and a disk-method volume integral is marked in part (b); both generic/application calculus skills are present.
All parts standardize a normal variable and invert normal probabilities; no conditional, sequence or broad-model method is independently marked.
The cosine rule and valid triangle range are primary; solving the resulting quadratic inequality is an independently used algebra secondary method.
The proof uses cross products and parallel/perpendicular vector relationships throughout; proof is not a separate taxonomy skill here.
Every part is vector line/plane work—parametric intersection, plane equations, normals, perpendicularity and angles—without a separate differentiation or inequality method.
Log laws and exponent manipulation solve the equation, while the domain check is supporting work; Exponents and logarithms is sufficient.
The first part counts no-match permutations and the repeated-game part uses a binomial model and moments; counting is a Number-and-algebra secondary.
The induction proof and derivative/tangent calculation are substantial and separately marked; trig notation and graph display are not extra skills.
Distance in the first half-second is the definite integral of velocity, evaluated by integration by parts; both application and integration labels are justified.
The graph supports the inequality setup, but the five marks solve and sign-analyze an inequality; algebra is primary and graphing is secondary.
Implicit differentiation and the vertical-tangent condition are the complete marked method, with no separately assessed graph or application technique.
The construction is entirely vector geometry, with the final triangle-area ratio adding a materially marked triangle-geometry method.
The three fruit prices come from a linear system; setting up and solving simultaneous equations is the only assessed method.
Differentiation handles the minimum, monotonicity and normal, while a disk integral handles volume; generic labels and radians are supporting notation.
Derivative/graph behavior is primary; the tangent-half-angle substitution and resulting cubic are separately marked trig and polynomial methods.
The loan and withdrawal values are geometric-series calculations; logarithms are not used as a distinct method in the markscheme.
The solution repeatedly conditions on events and applies conditional-probability identities; probability models adds no distinct marked method.
The two normal probability statements are standardized and solved simultaneously for the mean and standard deviation; Normal distribution is sufficient.
Right-triangle distances and the final cosine rule determine the yacht separation; all marks are triangle-geometry work.
The daily and weekly counts use Poisson/binomial reasoning and an expectation over 52 weeks; discrete random variables cover the marked work.
The substitution, differential and bounds evaluate an integral; trigonometry supplies the substitution but is not independently marked.
Continuity and differentiability at the join are enforced through a limit and derivative equality; Differentiation is the material skill.
The markscheme constructs an integrating factor, integrates the resulting equation and applies the initial condition; differential equations and integration are retained.
Limit comparison and endpoint analysis are the marked convergence methods; differentiation is not independently required.
The mean-value-theorem chord slope, derivative and solving for the two tangent points are all differentiation work; graphing illustrates it.
The derivative recurrence and Maclaurin coefficients support the limit and induction proof; limits/series and differentiation are the materially assessed methods.
